groups.title: Affix coinage
groups.note: The native full-sequence pass adds an affix. Some outputs retain only the first root; the second remains a generation input, not an audible part of the name.

candidates.name: icebreathium

groups.title: Andrew's latest directions
groups.note: Exploratory names from Andrew, with root explanations and fresh receipts. Existing uses and missing sources stay visible; no name was selected.

candidates.name: cryocean
candidates.explanation: Cryo and ocean meet at their shared o, putting the ice shell and the hidden water world into one compact word. It captures Enceladus's central contrast with very little explanation. A possible spoken reading is cry-OH-shun, though the spelling can invite other stresses; the existing-use receipt still applies.
candidates.editor_note: Andrew's new direction. Existing cryOcean research project and a registered .com are recorded; this name is not available across the checked sources.

candidates.name: zorbit
candidates.explanation: Zorb and orbit overlap around orb, so the playful sphere becomes a small world in motion. It is short enough to call across the installation and keeps both the physical object and the space theme audible. The lively sound is a strength, but the recorded existing-use result remains a separate concern.
candidates.editor_note: Andrew called this a strong direction. Existing exact uses include a moisture-control product, npm package, GitHub repositories and registered domains.

groups.title: Andrew's latest directions
groups.note: Exploratory names from Andrew, with root explanations and fresh receipts. Existing uses and missing sources stay visible; no name was selected.

candidates.name: cryzorcean
candidates.explanation: Cryo supplies ice, zorb supplies the vessel, and ocean supplies the hidden water world. The compressed zor seam places the sphere inside the cold-ocean idea, echoing the installation's transformation. A possible reading is cry-ZOR-shun; it has a strong center, though the three-root meaning and spelling take a little explanation.
candidates.editor_note: Andrew's exploratory three-root blend. No exact use found in the quoted web search and all five checked domains returned absence, but Bluesky and Reddit checks were unavailable. It remains unverified.
